rationale: Astra makes the grading decision concrete: rejecting an empty password is correct, but rejecting a valid password is a regression that blocks the patch. Its larger expected/actual labels read most clearly on a phone, and two passing checks lead explicitly to human review. Baseline is a useful follow-up on checking actual state rather than trusting Done; Fable shows how an incomplete grader can pass a broken artifact and how expanding the requirements exposes it.
findings: Astra 3.30–11.30s separates expected behavior, observed output, and grade: the same REJECT passes the empty-password case and fails valid login. This is more immediately actionable for a coding team than Baseline’s ticket predicate or Fable’s abstract test names.

Baseline 4.65s versus 16.45s shows the same Done message with different actual ticket states; only the state reaches the grader. Its retained trial result and 11.00s fixture reset introduce variability that the two patch revisions in Astra do not.

Fable 13.28–15.89s deliberately juxtaposes two failing regression tests with a passing narrow grader. At 19.00–22.83s it expands the required checks and rejects the same artifact, teaching grader quality rather than another agent retry.

Astra 23.80–26.70s ends with 2/2 passed and Human review, the strongest explicit limit on what these checks establish. Baseline 21.60–24.00s retains two trial outcomes; Fable 22.83–25.94s holds a failed artifact, without a release claim.

Fable throughout, especially 19.60–23.60s: revised 36px rows in wider stores replace cramped 26px type, and the required-checks label distinguishes predicates from results. Phone readability now passes, while Astra’s larger behavioral labels remain easier to scan.

Baseline 19.80s is the actual FAIL onset, corrected in its transcript; 21.60s only adds the trial number. Astra’s 10.60–10.90s and 23.10–23.40s evidence packets route around the grade text without obscuring it. All final cuts have matching decoded first/last frames and deliberate result holds.
contentVerdict: Keep as core: defining observable success, preserving required behavior, isolating trials, and retaining all attempts are early necessities for a team delegating engineering work to agents. The guide has a concrete exercise and appropriate limits on small samples, release readiness, grader reliability, and permissions. Its four primary sources were checked on 2026-10-19; retrieval dates were recorded and the budget-timeout versus environment-failure distinction was clarified. Harness engineering remains a reasonable prerequisite.
defectsFixed: Fable: enlarged test and grader text and stores for 350px legibility, repositioned gutter marks and verdict, and rerendered MP4/poster with original model provenance preserved.
Fable: labelled required predicates explicitly, changed task wording to fix login bug, and bounded the lesson to required existing behaviors.
Fable: aligned transcript and beat-sheet ending with the actual retained-title fade; removed an unverified perceptual loudest-sound claim; recorded editedBy and corrections metadata.
Baseline: corrected transcript FAIL onset to 19.80s and included fixture reset and numbered-result timing; retained original text in the review record.
Guide: added source retrieval dates and distinguished agent budget exhaustion from a broken evaluation environment.
limitations: Audio was analysed through full decode, peak levels, spectrograms, and signal windows around all 81 scheduled cues; it was not heard. Perceptual loudness and phone-speaker audibility were not tested.
Visual pacing was assessed from timestamped encoded contact sheets, native beat frames, 350px frames, and event timing, not continuous real-time playback or a learner study.

All three are illustrations, not measured agent experiments. Baseline’s two trials are not a reliability estimate; Astra’s patch revisions are not repeated samples; Fable shows only one trial per configuration.
Astra omits agent/harness internals; Baseline omits coding regressions; Fable uses abstract test names. The written guide is needed for the full workflow and technical boundaries.
Recommendation is saved for editorial review; no shared curriculum/build selection or publication operation was performed.
